account: It is eleven on day zero, and I am on my scheduled morning market walk. The only clearly unusual business I have heard about is the builder seeking a private meeting with the innkeeper near the inn at about 09:34. I heard the distant shout myself but could not distinguish its words; Townsfolk 30 and Townsfolk 20 later repeated the request. Their reports may come from the same shout, so they do not establish anything further. I saw the builder walking near the plaza at 10:45 carrying a lantern, and now see the innkeeper walking near the bridge holding an emerald. I have not witnessed a meeting or exchange. A private conversation could concern ordinary building work or inn business; I do not yet know its purpose and have no evidence of wrongdoing. Reports that the baker carried wheat at the bakery sound routine. My appointment book lists tea with the neighbour at a dockside cottage at three, but gives no exact cottage. The neighbour has personally confirmed the invitation; I have accepted and asked for directions, which remain unanswered. The secretary initially asked for my engagements despite the existing book, then acknowledged its entries and promised to verify the tea details. That seems an administrative uncertainty rather than proof of concealment. I want to learn more discreetly while keeping lunch at home at noon, accounts at one, tea at three, and office at four-thirty.
